criteria.description: CS (both directions) needs >= 2x fewer reads than the selected X-ABFT design (or X-ABFT misses F1 0.9 while CS reaches it) on >= 3 of 4 k at EACH of sigma 1% and 2%. This is the only version of the "fewer reads" claim the paper may print against X-ABFT.

criteria.source: section 12a expectation (untested) that the ratio decode fails under 2-4% read noise
criteria.description: X-ABFT, even with its design and repeat-and-average factor tuned per row, stays below F1 0.9 at sigma 4% for every k. If this fails the paper must not say the ratio decoder is noise-fragile; if it holds, the sentence is supported by a measurement instead of an expectation.

criteria.source: novelty wording: CS is the cheapest forward-readable cell-level localizer on this tile class
criteria.description: Kill the "fewer reads than prior-art cell-level localizers" wording if X-ABFT reaches F1 0.9 with fewer mean reads than CSB on >= 2 of 4 k at sigma 1% or at sigma 2%.
CSB held-out F1 below 0.8 on any 1-2% row (same floor as H8-kill; guards against a drifted join).

Strict-rule rows (row_ok_2x_x_strict), the paper-design arm (xpaper), forward-only ratios, undecodable fractions, native cost (tr_*, hr_*, n_test_vectors), selected designs, per-instance table (eval_instances.csv). X-ABFT's design target is 1-10% faults in a small block; ours is k <= 64 in 256 x 256, so no "X-ABFT fails" sentence is allowed without the regime caveat.
